column1: # Measured per-harness cost, in seconds, used ONLY to bin-pack the shards of
# .github/workflows/kani-full.yml. It is a scheduling hint, never evidence: a
# harness's verdict comes from the run, not from this file.
# PROVENANCE, stated because these numbers are easy to misread:
#   (one harness at a time, nothing else on the machine) of the then-240-harness
#   suite on a 14-core arm64 box, 2026-08-24, Kani 0.67.0. Solo numbers are used
#   deliberately: every later full sweep in this project ran many workers at once
#   and its wall times are 10-14x inflated by contention (measured:
#   solo vs 5890s under a 12-way sweep on a loaded box). Inflated numbers would
#   bin-pack fine but would be cited as costs by someone eventually, so they are
#   That run predates the F-02/F-03/F-04/Q/I2/K changes to src/v16.rs, which made
#   several close-path harnesses genuinely more expensive, and a GitHub hosted
#   runner is slower than that box. Both make these numbers OPTIMISTIC. That is
#   acceptable for bin-packing and is why the heavy harnesses are pinned by name in
#   heavy.txt rather than left to the packer.
#   237 of the 330 harnesses in the census appear here; the rest (added since
#   2026-08-24, or not in that suite) are packed at the 120 s default in
#   scripts/kani_census.py. A NEW harness therefore needs no edit here to be run --
#   the shard plan is derived from the census, not from this list.
# Regenerate: download the kani-full-census-tsv artefact from a green
# `Kani full census` run and keep columns 1 and 3 (harness, wall_s) -- but only
# from a run whose shards were not competing for cores, or the numbers will be
